grade.rationale: The stylesheet is coherent and uses sensible component structure, but the modal's default content-box height arithmetic can clip part of the scrollable region, and several labels use text sizes that are difficult to read. The highly compressed formatting also reduces maintainability.

summary: The primary correctness issue is that the dialog, header, and content heights include padding differently under the default content-box model, allowing the parent’s hidden overflow to obscure the bottom of long content. Very small fixed font sizes also impair readability. No coverage data was available, so test coverage remains unknown.

grade.rationale: The modal height calculations do not account for padding and borders under the default box model, which can clip long content.
Selectors are reasonably organized, but densely packing many rules onto each line makes changes, reviews, and debugging unnecessarily difficult.
Class names communicate intent, but compressed formatting and numerous very small typographic values make the visual design harder to inspect and reason about.
Error handling is largely inapplicable to a static stylesheet, and no invalid declarations or unsafe fallback behavior are evident.
Viewport-dependent sizing and overflow behavior require responsive visual or browser tests; no coverage evidence was supplied, so coverage is unknown.

findings.title: Content-box height calculations can clip the scrollable region
findings.description: The header has an explicit 66px height plus 24px of vertical padding, while the content has a viewport-derived max-height plus 32px of vertical padding. Under the default content-box model, their outer heights can exceed the dialog's max-height. Because the dialog uses overflow:hidden, the bottom of the content's own scrolling box can be clipped and become unreachable when the history is long. This only works safely if an undocumented global border-box rule happens to apply.
findings.recommendation: Make the dialog a column flex container with box-sizing:border-box, give the header a non-growing size, and use flex:1; min-height:0; overflow:auto on the content. Alternatively, explicitly include padding and borders in every height calculation, though the flex approach is less fragile.

findings.title: Multiple interface labels are rendered at only 8–9px
findings.description: Metadata and definition labels repeatedly use 8px or 9px text. At normal browser zoom these sizes are difficult to read, especially on high-density or small displays, and uppercase transformation further reduces legibility.
findings.recommendation: Use the project's accessible typography tokens where available and raise secondary labels to a readable baseline, generally at least 11–12px. Validate the dialog at browser zoom levels up to 200%.
